title: Constant-tower direct image and limit normalization for identified ring sheaves
statement:
Let $f:(\mathscr X,R_X)\to(\mathscr Y,R_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi presented by small sites, with a specified ring isomorphism $f^{-1}R_Y\cong R_X$. Module pullback $F=f^*$ is exact and left adjoint to module direct image $G=f_*$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the ringed-topos convention [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], and strict inverse sequences indexed by $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$.
Let $\mathcal G=RG$ and $\mathcal G^{\rm Tow}=R(G^{\rm Tow})$, with evaluation comparisons and $a_M:\mathcal G R\lim_XM\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim_Y\mathcal G^{\rm Tow}M$ normalized as in [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison]. There is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$\chi_K:\Delta_Y\mathcal G K\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal G^{\rm Tow}\Delta_XK.$$
On a K-injective representative $J$ it is the equality $\Delta_YGJ=G^{\rm Tow}\Delta_XJ$. Under the normalized evaluation comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-tower-derived-evaluation-normalization], every evaluation of $\chi_K$ is the identity. The canonical maps $R\lim_T\Delta_TK\cong K$ of the strict-tower derived limit [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] identify $R\lim_Y(\chi_K)^{-1}a_{\Delta_XK}$ with $1_{\mathcal G K}$. The assertion applies to arbitrary ring sheaves $R_T$, not just constant coefficient rings. Under $F^{\rm Tow}\Delta_Y=\Delta_XF$, it also satisfies the strict counit equation $\varepsilon^{\rm Tow}_{\Delta_XK}\circ F^{\rm Tow}(\chi_K)=\Delta_X(\varepsilon_K)$.

source.place: Tag 0A07, lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim: diagram-topos proof, specialized to constant towers

proof.text: Use small-module-diagrams-grothendieck on the AsSmall model of the inverse-sequence category and transport along AsSmall.equiv; the module category itself is Grothendieck by the existing module-sheaf instance. Apply kinjective-functorial-existence to obtain K-injective resolutions in both categories. Constants, evaluations and levelwise F are exact by levelwise kernels and cokernels, and their exact derived functors have the specified localization factorizations.

Construct evaluation at op 0 left adjoint to constants explicitly: the inverse to evaluation of a tower map sends g:T_0 -> A to the maps T(n -> 0) followed by g. Naturality and the inverse identities follow from functoriality and naturality. Since evaluation is exact, right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective makes the constant complex on every K-injective complex K-injective.

source.place: Tag 08BJ, lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives; explicit adjunction for the terminal index 1

proof.text: An additive functor sends quasi-isomorphisms between K-injectives to quasi-isomorphisms: use kinjective-hom-derived to write such a map as a homotopy equivalence and map that equivalence termwise. The existing cochain K-injective derivability structure therefore shows that each specified right-derived unit is invertible on K-injectives. This uses the supplied right-derived functors, without constructing additional derived operations.

For the constant interchange h:G followed by Delta_S is isomorphic to Delta_R followed by G^Tow, form two units with common source QG followed by D(Delta_S): the first is D(Delta_S)(eta); the second is the constant localization factorization, Q(h), etaT on Delta_R, and the inverse source factorization. Both are invertible on K-injectives by steps 2 and 3. The derivability criterion makes both pairs right-derived pairs, so rightDerivedUnique constructs chi. Its factorization equation gives the representative identity, in fact on every complex.

Write the evaluation expression as a natural endotransformation of RG. On QI, precompose by the invertible eta_I, insert the localization factorization of constant evaluation, and substitute the representative equation for chi. Naturality of beta moves the constant localization factor across beta; hbeta on the K-injective constant tower then reduces the expression to eta_I. Cancel it. Every derived object is isomorphic to QI for a K-injective I, so naturality extends equality to every object.

source.place: Tag 0A07, lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim, first proof: common direct-image composite on diagram topoi, specialized to constant towers

proof.text: The ordinary constLimAdj unit is invertible because the constant functor over the connected index category is fully faithful. Form its degreewise image followed by etaR (respectively etaS) on constants and the inverse constant localization factorization. Step 2 and the unit computation of step 3 make this transformation invertible on K-injectives. Derived uniqueness against the identity functor constructs bR and bS and gives their required localization equations on every complex.

Compare RG(bR) followed by a with bS followed by LS(chi) as natural transformations. On QI precompose with eta_I and postcompose with LS(RT of the constant factorization). Insert hbR, hbS, hchi, and the supplied ha, and use naturality of the derived units. The remaining equality is the chain-map equality G(uR) followed by c equals uS followed by lim(h). Prove it degreewise by the limit projections using hc and the ordinary constLimAdj unit. Cancel the invertible factors and extend by naturality. Compose with LS(chi inverse) and bS inverse to get the displayed limit identity.

source.place: Tag 0A07, lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim, first proof: common direct-image composite on diagram topoi, specialized to constant towers

proof.text: Apply each supplied derived Hom formula to the ordinary chain-level counit. Its transpose is the identity, so applying inverse derived transposition gives D(F)(eta) followed by the derived counit equal to the exact factorization followed by Q of the ordinary counit, and likewise for towers. Compare the requested counit arrows naturally. On QI precompose by D(F^Tow)(D(Delta_S)(eta_I)) and postcompose by the constant localization factorization. Insert hchi, both counit formulas, and the factorization of the specified exact pullback interchange. The result is the degreewise equality that the tower counit on a constant complex is the constant ordinary counit. Cancel and extend to all derived objects by naturality.

Checks: (1) the diagram categories for J=pt and N>=1^op are Grothendieck for any ring sheaf, and levelwise exactness makes Delta, e_n and F^Tow exact; (2) e_1 -| Delta checked by hand (u_n = u_1 o M(n->1)), and right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective applies with u=Delta, v=e_1; (3) G preserves K-injectives because F is exact, and G^Tow Delta_X J = Delta_Y GJ holds strictly; (4) chi = eta_{G^Tow} o (Delta_Y eta_G)^{-1} has the right types, is invertible, and extends to D through the K-injective Hom bijection; (5) the beta normalization at Delta_X J gives e_n(chi)=1; (6) lim Delta J = J, and b is invertible by K-injectivity; (7) a, being the common-composite comparison, is represented by 1_{GJ} because all three inputs are K-injective, and the equation's types check; (8) both counits are represented by eps^0_J and Delta_X eps^0_J, and the tower equation is the localization of an equality of chain maps, not an inference from evaluations. Sources: Stacks 0A07 (sites-cohomology l.5150, first proof); tags 08BJ/070K/070Y/070I/09T5/079P/015F match tags/tags; the blueprint main-20261015 sk-prop-pbc-complete last sentence is the from.place; no SGA.
